goal: measure the 3x3-DENSE-chunk decomposition against exp16a's all-pointwise one, on identical block-1 data
mechanism: 1xK -> ceil(K/3) dense 3x3 dispatches, each a 3x3 kernel with only the middle row populated; infeat_addr += 3*c*ch_im_in; H padding 1/1 native (legal in 3x3 mode); streamin for chunks 1..N-1; int32 out
performance_finding: dense 3x3 chunks are 1.15x FASTER than all-pointwise (1,362,823 vs 1,567,096) despite the MAC-cycle model predicting ~3x SLOWER. The model assumed the array is the bottleneck; at this size it is not -- 6 dispatches instead of 16 means 6 instead of 16 job setups and 5 instead of 15 int32 streamin round-trips through L1. The workload is DMA/setup-bound, not MAC-bound.
correctness_status: single chunk (no streamin) already wrong: 431/1536, ALL diffs +-1 LSB on outputs in range [-2,3]. conf0 differs from the working pointwise variant ONLY in filter mode (0x40), so the configuration is right and the datapath differs. Zero-weight rows should cancel exactly (w_u=128, Wmin=-128 -> w_u+Wmin=0); why they do not is unresolved.

weight_cost.note: 3.4x more weight memory: 6 of every 9 tap slots are zeros
